Overall, Dr. Schech was one of the best professors that I ever had and I would 100% recommend anyone to take her class just to get her as a professor.

Friedman is seriously not as bad as everyone says. His exams are fairly difficult but they are very similar to the practice exams he provides. He has a generous curve at the end of the year; he said that a 75% in the class would be an a overall at the end of the semester. He also takes time to answer questions during class and answers them thoroughly, so if you are confused just ask him. He doesn't record lectures which is kinda annoying considering the class is at 8 am, but he always posts notes which is helpful. I didn't take AP chem but I'm doing fine in this class, you just have to ask questions, do a lot of review even if you don't have an exam coming up, and use his practice exams to study, and you'll be fine.

DO. NOT. TAKE. This professor is single-handedly crushing my hopes and dreams. He cannot teach to save his life; he is insulting- don't ask him questions if you don't want to be made a fool. If you don't have a solid chemistry background you will fail. There was not a single topic he covered enough to make me feel comfortable. This class is quite literally self-taught with a side of insults. Awful teacher, awful person, worst professor in my three years of college.

Honestly, I enjoyed the class and didn't think the material was too hard. He can go a little fast sometimes and explain some things more complicated than they need to be, but if you go to class and the GSS sessions, you should be fine. I will say, taking AP Chem in high school gives you a HUGE advantage. I've done really well in the course because I am already super familiar with the material from AP Chem last year.

I love Dr. Stocker for gen chem. She explains everything so clearly and uses such niche examples. She keeps it 100% real about what is expected of you and how to do well in the course. Gen chem is always going to be hard no matter what professor you take and you just have to know that. It is all about the work you put in! Dr. Stocker posts a bunch of problem sets and practice tests for you to do, and if you use these resources the more likely you are to succeed. Dr. Stocker doesn't record lectures, but you should be there anyway!! I highly recommend.

Canvas is a little unorganized and yes the reflection quizzes are hard, but your experience really depends on how good your TA is. I've never met Guest, but there are a lot of typos in Canvas and in the quizzes. The TA's are not super hard graders when it comes to lab reports, and I had a really good TA, so I enjoyed lab and did pretty well on it. Busy work and needs to be more than 1 credit, but not that hard.

Don’t take this class if you weren’t born with a PHD in chemistry. Studying homework, practice problems, and past exams will not help, as the exams are more about how to understand his word problems than the content. I can get behind the fact that lectures are not recorded and notes are illegible, since paying attention in lecture can fix this, however the structure of the exams, especially closer to the end of the semester, makes them almost impossible to pass. The grade cutoffs are good, however once students withdraw from the class (a lot do), they decrease. It seems like he wants to see low averages on these exams. I know it’s a weed out class, but exams should be about understanding and mastering concepts and math. Application is very important, however when problems are so far off of what we learned, it isn’t effective.

The fact that this man has a five star review from this semester is absolutely insane to me, and inspired me to write this. Sure, he's an alright guy, one might even argue he's pretty nice outside of grading. I don't view him in that way though, as he spent an entire lecture explaining to us how it isn't his job to teach. I understand reviewing and studying on our own is important, but for someone who's just trying to pass gen chem and is not pre med, the amount of work needed to even pass this class, let alone do well, is unacceptable. The class average is failing, and the most common score on the first exam was a 20/80, and all of the averages so far have been failing and typically around 50%. None of us know if we will pass or fail because he doesn't have a curve built in (which is something many chem professors do). His tests are much harder than the practice problems and practice tests he provides, so it's nearly impossible to do well on the actual exams, which make up around 80 percent of our grades. He might have been a good TA, but compared to other professors he has no idea how to run a class, which is intensified by this being an introductory class that should not be this insanely difficult to pass.

I honestly don't know how Dr. Lascio is getting five star ratings. Although he is a decently nice person and does try to answer questions as best he can, my experience in his class has not been great. Every single exam has had a failing score as the class average. I personally believe that this is a reflection of Dr. Lascio's teaching, as I have heard other chem131 sections having average test scores of at least 70-75%. The only reason I am expecting a C+ is because of the hopes I have that he will curve this class. Also, a girl in my class emailed him about her concerns about our second midterm because everyone did so bad on the first one (average of a 52%), and he pulled up her email in front of the entire lecture hall and picked it apart for a good 25-30 minutes. He claimed she gave him permission but I still found it a little off-putting that he did that and it also wasted time in the class that could have been used for reviewing material for the second exam. He also says that if we pass the final exam, he will automatically pass us with a C-, which infers the final is basically going to be impossible. I study for every exam for at least a week before, and I have only passed one. Praying that I can pass this class.

There are pros and cons of Dr. Friedman
Pros:
-He wants you to learn the content, not just get an A. However (this is a con to some degree), learning the content might result in a C or a B
-He remembers your name if and only if you introduce yourself. This will be helpful, trust me.
-The curve is very generous, but don't let that fool you into not trying. The exams are HARD
-If you show that you are there to learn, not grovel for an A, then he will put an effort to make sure you learn
-He has his quirks and he's very straightforward/blunt. This could seem passive-aggressive or rude, but its how he is.
Cons:
-He doesn't record lecture, however, as past reviews have said: if you attend lecture and pay attention you don't have to worry about this
-His class is a morning class, ALWAYS. If you don't want to attend a morning class, don't pick Dr. Friedman's lectures
-The exams are TOUGH. Especially the third exam. That's just a fact of college tho.
-Lectures are fast paced BUT if you ask to go back, he will go back to a previous slide

How to succeed:
-Sadly, I feel the need to say this but GO TO LECTURE. Yes, its early morning. Yes, you are tired. Yes, I don't think you want to be here. But attend lecture anyway. You chose this class (even if you didn't and it was a marriage of convenience), attend lecture. The next 2 relate to this point.
-DO NOT RELY ON HIM POSTING NOTES. This ties in with the first point. If he sees a phone out in class, lecture notes won't be posted.
-DO NOT RELY ON THE TEXTBOOK. He teaches stuff that are not from the textbook. If you rely on it completely and don't attend lecture, you will not succeed
-GO TO GSS. I couldn't because it clashed with my lab and scholars class, but GSS problems are ALWAYS posted so there is no excuse to not practice
-GO TO OFFICE HOURS. Dr. Friedman literally teaches one class and it is this class. Go to him. He is really helpful and kind. He will focus on your questions in detail and has no issue re-explaining them several times. 
-GO TO DISCUSSION. Discussion exists so you can ask questions. GO TO THEM.
-If you are in HS, this is for you, if not, next one is for you. If you are in HS, TAKE AP CHEM. IT WILL HELP
-If you are starting university, this is for you. KHAN ACADEMY and THE ORGANIC CHEMISTRY TUTOR will literally save your life if you want to prep early for this class.

So now, you might be thinking: Ah heck naw! I do want to say that Dr. Friedman is a really good professor. You just need to put in the extra work to succeed. It is college after all, you won't be spoon fed anything. Dr. Friedman is a really chill person and while his tests are tough and his teaching style is slightly old fashioned, HE DOES PREPARE YOU FOR ORGO CHEM. Also, because of how difficult i found this course to be, I do want to say Dr. Friedman will teach you certain things about yourself that none of my classes taught me:
-Exams beat you up, but you need to get up, improve, and move on
-You will only know if you are learning if the learning is painful
-You will get flesh wounds from college, its part of the experience. Better to get it early so you can improve later on!
-If I wanted an easy gen chem class, then I'd have learned these lessons much later which would have def been more detrimental for me.

All in all, take this class if you want. Dr. Friedman is a good professor and a good person. His focus is you learning, not to get an A. I want to say something final: I think that all the pain and beating I went through during this course was worth it. If I had another 1000 tries to do this again, I'd take Dr. Friedman's class every single time. Hope that helps.

He’s a great professor. He’s super approachable and friendly and definitely recommend him out of all the other professors in the chem department. Just a chill causal guy. Plus his blazers over his graphic tee shirts that he’d wear is actually so fire: Chemistry is just extremely difficult but he does his best to help you and is a very understanding guy. The curve is pretty big so you’ll probably be okay but go to the gss sessions and his office hours! Going to these and showing up to the lectures will save you. The textbook also helps. There’s only 5 grades this whole semester so everything counts. He also responds to emails really quickly which is absolutely amazing shout out to him. And the memes he puts on the slides are actually funny and up to date. That’s not that important but a great plus. 

The practice midterm is decently similar to the real midterm but things change so you actually have to go over all the slides and notes because there may be things on there that actually wasn’t on the practice exam. That caught me off on the first exam. The midterms in general are actually awful. But that’s in every class with any professor. Chemistry is just hard, but he really made it bearable.

Dr. Stocker is a great professor for lectures and she always provides many practice problems. She does not record her lectures but they are worthwhile to attend. Her lectures mainly consist of going over practice problems so you know how to do them while studying. I plan on taking her for orgo next semester because she is reliable and kind.

The hate is unwarranted. CHEM131 is a very difficult course and, in my opinion, Professor Friedman does a great job at explaining the content. His sense of humor is very sarcastic, which can come off as mean at times, but he always means well. He's very enthusiastic about the subject, and always willing to answer questions. He moves quickly but is more than willing to slow down if you are struggling to write notes. He always kept us up-to-date on our pace, whether we were ahead or behind etc. The exams are difficult, but very reflective of the content.

In terms of assignments, you have one digital Pearson homework about once a week. This is my only grievance, as these are insanely difficult and tedious. Additionally, the online textbook doesn't cover half the content in the assignments, so you either have to lose points by accepting hints, Google it, or just wing it. These homeworks are only 15% of your grade though, so don't stress *too* hard. The other 85% comes from exams, so make sure to study hard and use the practice exams and GSS worksheets to their full advantage.

Overall, I think he is one of the better CHEM131 professors, and I would recommend taking him if you need the class.

Dr. Lascio is a solid professor. A lot of people complain that he isn't a good teacher, but I think if you show up to lecture and take notes, he explains everything pretty well. We had 3 midterm exams and the averages were around 50-60% for each. However with his curve for this semester (which is based on the class average), an 80+ is an A and a 70+ is a B. In addition to our midterm grades, we had around 9 homework assignments that added up to be 80 points, the same amount of points as each midterm exam, which really helped people's grades. I'd recommend actually trying to do the homework problems even though they're often way more challenging than the exam questions, because they help you become more familiar with the content. In terms of studying, look through all the slideshows he posts and make sure you can do every single problem he's done in class. He also posts a practice exam for each midterm, which is relatively similar to the real exams, although they seemed to be a little easier. His exams are fair, but for a lot of people time was a challenge. He likes to include trick questions, which can be frustrating, but very simple if you know your stuff. Lastly, he can be a little unhelpful when you ask questions in class, but I truly think he wants all his students to succeed!

She’s fine. Explains concepts pretty well. But you can’t afford to miss class at all. Even looking at friends notes won’t rly help u because the slides she posts are not the ones she annotates during class. Her practice exams and what she teaches are similar to her exams, which I like.

Took this class as a part of freshman connection in fall '25. Stump is a great teacher to get you acquainted with the differences between high school and college, it is a lecture style class with a very traditional teaching style that is easily digestible. With a simple chemistry background that you should have received from HS, this class is very easy. She assigns weekly homework on pearson, and they are forgiving with missed problems. I had 3 exams in the semester, and they were no trouble. Take decent notes, pay attention and you should be fine.

I would say Dr. Lascio is very nice, but I’m not sure whether it’s the chemistry curriculum at UMD or his class specifically that is extremely difficult. This is coming from someone who took chemistry in high school and enjoyed it, so I do have some background knowledge in the subject. That being said, even with some foundational knowledge in chemistry, I found this course to be difficult, especially the exams. On our three midterms, the  averages were 42, 51, and 43.

I'm pretty sure this was her first year teaching and obviously there were some flaws but overall she was a good professor. She did struggle with answering questions, not really explaining what the student was asking, but going to office hours for more help is definitely worth it. I would say that her exams are fair for the content that she covers and her study guides are reflective of what will be on the exam. She assigns online homeworks each week which aren't hard and are great practice for exams. I don't think she curved any tests but that was because the class average was 70-80 each time. Overall, she is a caring professor and if you can take her, do it!

This class is hard af but Dr. Lascio doesn't really do anything to make it harder than it needs to be. His slides are fun, lectures and discussion are good, and the GSS is pretty helpful. I would give 5 stars but I think the exams are just a little bit too hard. A lot of the questions feel like they're trying to trick you on purpose by asking about super small and insignificant pieces of information, and some of the free response questions are just brutal. I'm pretty sure there was one on our second exam that 3/~500 people got right, so that's about how hard we're dealing with. All that said though, this class is 100% passable since he incorporates a very generous curve at the end where you only need a 50 to get a C and if you pass the final he'll just pass you anyway. Overall, hard class, but Dr. Lascio isn't to blame for that.

Schech is a really good professor; she provides a lot of resources to help you understand the material. During her lectures, she uses analogies to break things down and make sure you understand. That being said, her third exam was very hard and lengthy. I know many students who couldn't finish that exam. She definitely did it to bring the class average down, which was an A- at the time.

Shes super sweet and a great teacher. She posts practice exams for the first three exams and makes sure her students understand the content. However, the material on the exams are MUCHHH harder than what we practiced in class and on the practice exams. So prepare to study a lotttt!!!

Dr. Schech 10/10 would recommend. She made chemistry understandable and is super nice. She records all of her lectures and posts slides ahead of time and notes afterwards. The Canvas page is well organized, practice exams and answer keys are posted, as well as discussion and GSS worksheets and keys. Homeworks are on Pearson, basically completion grades. They can be kind of time-consuming and annoying, but they’re not too bad and I think they prepare you well for exams. HW and three exams plus the final are the only grades in the class, so do the HW. Compared to other 131 teachers, it sounds like hers are easier (class average around 80% as opposed to 40). One exam had an extra credit point for naming some songs you like. 
Dr. Schech is also just a cool and nice person, everything she teaches makes sense and she always uses analogies about her kids or her sister to help you understand. Discussion is optional attendance; many people don’t go but I go to force myself to do the practice problems.

TLDR Schech is probably the best CHEM131 lecturer you could get, grades are easy, lectures are recorded.

Dr. Schech is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. I came into Gen Chem 1 not confident at all because I always thought I was not good at chemistry. The way she teaches completely changed that for me. She explains why everything works and she uses stories and real examples that actually stay in your mind. Her class does not feel like a typical lecture. It feels like a place where you can ask questions and really understand what is going on.

What I appreciate the most is how much she cares about her students. She always makes time to answer questions, she checks in on people, and she wants to make sure everyone truly understands the material. I have seen her stay after class helping students one on one. Because of her, I went from being scared of chemistry to actually enjoying it and feeling confident in it.

If you put in the effort, she will support you completely. I am genuinely grateful that I took her class. She is a gem of a professor and I would recommend her to anyone taking Gen Chem 1.

REALLY NOT BAD GUYS!!! I took AP Chem so i had a bit of background, but I don't consider myself a Chem person at all. I had his 8 am and missed probably 3 lectures?? People who say he doesn't teach well probably don't think about how it's a LOT of content, but only 50 minutes long. I thought he did a great job and gave example problems for everything, which helped. The TA i had for this was useless, so going to the discussion was a waste of time because the worksheets she gave sucked. The GSS leaders had AMAZING worksheets i used to study, but i didn't go to the GSS just did the worksheets after. He gives you practice exams for every midterm which were SO helpful not only with showing how he writes questions but also just all the content (def do all 3 he gives for each midterm). People who do poorly, I'm not sure why. I feel like they just didn't prepare well for a COLLEGE CLASS- this is college after all, it isn't supposed to be super easy. He says to study everyday, i honestly just retook the class notes everyday which takes 20 minutes and then I start studying for the exams 3 nights before? I got an A on both midterm 1 and 2, and a C on the third (but he does say it is the hardest). I would say if you score a A/B on two of the exams and a C on the other one, you should end with an A because of his huge grade curve. People say he doesnt prepare you for orgo well so i guess well see, cant really comment on that.

Only take this professor if you absolutely have to and have no other choice. I understand that chemistry will always be a hard class, regardless of who you take it with, but there is genuinely no winning in this class. Everyone thinks that people who do bad in this class just "didn't try hard enough" or just "blame the professor", but you can do all the homework, a ton of practice problems, and ALL the past exams, understand everything completely, and still get a bad grade on the exams. In his lectures, he goes too fast, brushes over topics that will probably be questions on the exam worth 14 points, and just explains a lot of theory without actual application. He will stop for questions, but he will make you feel bad if you ask something that he considers simple or not hard to understand (which is everything). If you do have to take his class, go to GSS (this probably saved me), go to discussion as the grad TA is super helpful, watch a lot of organic chemistry tutor, and just practice, practice, practice.

If knowing proofs and knowing the why helps you learn, then he's great. Sure he moves a little fast, but with high school chem as a background, you should be ok if you study. However, if proofs and knowing the why sounds not helpful, he's not for you. Other chem courses exams will stop after an application problem, but his exams have a follow up of "why?" So while others may stop at "what is the molecular geometry of this?" his will go "why does the lone pair go here and not here?" and while others may stop at "what is the final temperature of hot glassed placed in cold water?" he will ask "what would happen to the final temperature if the glass broke?" Basically he dives deep into the why and expects you to keep up and understand not only how to use the material but why.
However, he is an unempathetic, unpleasant person. I struggle with mental health, and not in a "oh im sad and lazy and don't want to go to class" way, but in a clinically depressed way. I understand it is not an excuse to ask for higher grades or special treatment, neither of which I asked for. Having missed a few lectures, I went to his office hours for help. For a quick run over of what I missed and a walk through of maybe 2 problems. He basically said "you're fucked, now you have to learn old material and new material, go to class you idiot." He said he had no experience with mental health struggles and quite literally made me cry. I got an 87 on that exam, no thanks to him. His lack of empathy and simply unprofessional reply motivated me to get a good score as a fuck you to him. Anyways, don't expect him to help. He's a good teacher depending on your learning style, but he sucks ass as a person.

Amazing professor. 
-approachable and kind 
-digestible lectures (especially as someone who struggles with chem)
-fair exams (practice exams are so helpful, lots of resources)
I had her for chem over the summer and she was honestly great. I had an 89.something and that ended me with an A+. She took time to stay after class to answer questions and her tests were fair.

Taking this over the summer probably wasn't the best idea. I grasped the pace of the course while taking it. Orgo requires a lot of memorization, which does not couple well with a short amount of time. Also, a solid foundation of it is key to succeeding in Orgo 2. Professor Koppel is not as bad as I thought. She cares and does her best. However, it's just difficult to sit through 10 hours of lecture consecutively in a week, alongside the lab. Not recommended over the summer!

lascio is great!!! he's a great prof i'm just failing because i'm bad at chem lol. anyway yeah idk what grade i'll get but we'll see. lascio is great and chill he's funny. 4 stars because for one lecture which was an exam review right before midterm 2 he was just reviewing a student's email and i was like damn...this is lowk unproductive....but yeah he's a chill guy i'd recommend anyway. just because he's cool. just don't be like me and actually lock in lol...i'm so happy i'm not pre-med....

In my opinion Friedman is kinda funny. But! this class genuinely sucked the life out of me. The homework's took me 2-3 hours but that might have been a me problem. He doesn't record lectures, only posts notes but they can be hard to understand without context. He shifts the grading scale so a 60 is lowkey passing and a high 70 or low B is probably about an A. I will say though even with that, the average of the last midterm was a 47 and I got a 45. Overall I got a 33 on the first, a 59 on the second and a 45 on the last one. There were a lot of things he never fully went over in class though. For example I'm not sure if he ever actually explained what the general charges of elements were on a periodic table which is pretty basic and foundational stuff. If you expect him to actually teach, don't get your hopes up. He's very good when it comes to introducing a topic and then sometimes he'll do a couple examples but if you actually want to understand you gotta teach yourself. If you're good at that kind of thing and you did good in AP chem in high school you should be fine. Obviously I'm not good at teaching myself and I never took AP chem. The GSS people were really nice though. Half star for the jokes, another for the GSS. But I'm definitely failing this class. Please don't take this class if haven't taken any kind of AP chem class before. Even if you have no other choice don't do it. Save yourself. Run and never look back. :(

Everyone saying Friedman isn't as bad as everyone say's is either saying absolute BS or is glazing him- he has his favorites. This is my third chem class due to being a transfer student and taking it in high school and this is literally the hardest class I've ever taken. His exams are genuinely horrible, he one time wrote on one "I know we didn't cover this in class"... He words the exams so bad so half the time you have no idea what to even do, and the exams are essentially ur entire grade. The homework's were tough, but 100 times easier than exam material. No matter what I did to try and get through this class, it never helped. Unless you have the time and energy to make chem your entire semesters focus and you're willing to pay 15 dollars a month for the pearson plus textbook, you are probably screwed!

Dr.Lascio is genuinely a great teacher. His lectures are very informative and he’s very accommodating when it comes to scheduling regrades, office hours, and exam reviews. He replies to emails very quickly and actually cares about the wellbeing of his students. Discussion session is optional but has good resources for exam prep. Study by doing the homework problems until you fully understand them and by reviewing concepts in the lectures slides.

Lascio is a very engaging lecturer and tries to make his class as interesting as chemistry can be. However, he is a petty guy who will blame the entire class for failing and not anything else 😭. I remember that during an exam review session, he spent the entire time arguing with a student who wrote a genuine email about how they were concerned about the exam. He had this email up on the board and literally said “I’m trying to make eye contact with whoever wrote this,” then proceeded to nitpick everything wrong with it. Other times he’s really nice and will answer your questions without condescension (it’s kinda hard to tell what mood he’s in). He curves your grade at the end, and his exams are VERY difficult. Definitely doable, just a very hard subject.

I am a non stem major who took this course for the gened since I switched in late. So as a moral masochist, this sucks. Learned more from the homeworks and practice exams than his class. Only reason I did good was because I am proficient with math. It's possible, but if you are buns with math, good luck.
Take her.
Take her with no question.

If you can take Dr Schech, please do. I haven't touched chemistry since high school but I understood all of the material from this semester completely. She is a great lecturer and makes it worth it to just go to class instead of watching recordings. She gives 1 HW once a week, that I would recommend doing as they are super helpful for practice. If you actually do the HWs they do take pretty long but its worth it. I never went to discussion as it's not required after the first one. I went to office hours once or twice and she was extremely helpful and super sweet. I did the best on the midterm that I went to her office hours to ask questions. Her exams: they're definitely not easy but doable. I would say they are harder than the practice exams she posts but not by a terrible amount. Midterm 3 was pretty hard though. The final wasn't terrible but I would definitely study for it, as well as the midterms. Overall, I love her teaching style and she definitely cares about this class, so if you can take her, you should.

A really great professor who did a great job of making the material understandable and providing many ways to review/practice. He obviously cares about his students, and has been very accommodating in holding review sessions and extending homeworks. However, I will say this class was difficult and his practice exams were not a true representation of how hard the actual exams would be. The average on each exam was usually around 50%, and because he does not put all grades in and apply the curve until the end of the semester it is hard knowing what grade you can expect. Still, the curve for our class was over 10%, so as long as you can get above average on the exams you can get a good grade.

He is not a good lecturer and does not take the time to solve questions or clarify things for students. He answers every question he receives in class with attitude and makes it seem like the student is completely dumb for asking whatever it was. His method of presenting is not very good in my opinion, he just scribbles on a blank page for 50 minutes and it would be a lot more helpful if he had like pre-written slides that he just expanded on in class. His exams were nothing like the homework or lectures (coming from someone who didn't miss a single one) and he always said if you go to every class then you'll be fine, which was not true at all because I was always taking notes and still had to study for hours just to do mediocre on each test. Also, I find it really weird how he wants the averages for each test to be around a 55% because it just seems like he is expecting everyone to fail and instead of making the exams more like his teaching, he just doesn't care. His TA for this semester was also completely unhelpful, the discussion session was maybe 5-10 minutes long with answering 2-3 questions that were barely related to lecture and there was never any review for exams or any extra resources. I would avoid taking him if you don't have a PhD in chemistry.

I liked her a lot as a professor, i can see why many don’t however. She is kind of unapproachable and goes pretty fast in lecture lol. However she is definitely one of the better chem professors out of the options available. She gives plenty of old practice exams which will tell you how heavily weighted certain topics are going to be, my one complaint is that the final had a lot of new material on it that was recently learned which seemed disproportionate and i felt as if there wasn’t enough time to practice it. Curve is also good

Dr. Lascio is a very kind and approachable professor who responds to emails very quickly (for the most part) and is always willing to help students. His tests were relatively fair. He doesn't curve exams, only your final grade so its difficult to know how you're doing in the class. Overall, I recommend him.

Dr. Schech is a MUST for CHEM131. From the beginning of the semester, Dr. Schech sets a very generous curve: 94.5 = A+. 89.5 = A. 84.5 = A-, and so forth. This curve does not rise throughout the semester even if the class is performing above average. Additionally, her exams are extremely fair. All you have to do is go to lectures (or watch her Panopto recordings: there is no class attendance), do the homework (which is basically a free weekly A), and complete her practice exams before each assessment, and I can almost guarantee you will succeed. Another note, her practice exams are very similar to the exams she gives in class, and she is not the type of teacher to "throw in surprises." 

Another note: I really enjoyed Dr. Schech's teaching style. She uses fun analogies to help you understand content and takes her time to explain each topic. Whenever I was asked which chem professor I had, and I responded Dr. Schech, I would always receive a "bruh, lucky, I wish." Overall, I would definitely recommend taking her course.

It is very evident Dr. Friedman is knowledgeable on the subject. He also teaches with interest which is nice especially since it was at 8 in the morning. I found exams to be a lot more difficult than what I saw from other professors teaching the same course but the curve really helps. Also, the exams are a lot like the practice he offers! I would recommend doing practice problems after each lecture, going to GSS, and asking him for help the second you get confused.

I really enjoyed this class. Dr Friedman is a funny and kind professor who wants his students to do well. Yes it is a hard class but you just have to put in the work. He provides homework, old exams, and practice problems. The exams are challenging but if you look at his past exams you will be able to understand easily. I recommend going to GSS whenever it is offered, it helps 100%. The averages on tests are low but he curves generously with a 75 being an A.

First off, loved his class. He's a great professor and explains things well verbally, but you will have to attend his lectures if you want to get much out of his class. He doesn't post recordings unless he's sick or the lecture was virtual, and there's a lot he elaborates on out loud that you'll miss out on if you only read the lecture notes. His tests are pretty straight-forward, but you can't just memorize equations and expect to pass because he specifically constructs the exams to avoid students doing that. He's willing to do regrades and everyone I know got at least a couple extra points from any regrade request they submitted, and the homework assignments combined are worth as much as a midterm so if you don't do well on those, the homework can boost your grade. He even took an entire chapter off our second exam because people complained it was too hard (we hadn't gotten to the chapter in class, but it'd been posted for over a week at the time). The class is hard, duh, it's gen chem, but he's great. If he ever teaches CHEM131 again he's probably one of the best options, but after our class I don't think he's going to teach it again. I know he'll teach CHEM132 and CHEM135 next semester; can't say much about him as a lab coordinator, but I hear good things about his CHEM135. My only gripe with his whole class was that he waits until a week or so before an exam to give you the practice exam and study guide, so if you have a lot going on at the same time as his exam it's hard to space out preparation.

Pretty good teacher overall. Goes through slides in class to teach. She uploads her slides to canvas, but doesn't upload her annotations that she makes in class. She also doesn't record the lectures making it very important to go to class. I liked how she explained a lot of the concepts though since she made it a lot easier for me to understand. Her exams are somewhat difficult, but fair. All of the content on the exams she goes over in class. I think the best way to succeed in this class is practicing and using all of the resources and practice problems. If you do this you will pass pretty easily. Good teacher overall and I recommend taking her!

This man is actually one of the worst teachers I've ever had. He assumes that everyone has their PHD in chemistry. Zooms through lecture, the TA I had for discussion was completely useless, would literally show up to class and go over one problem and allow us to leave. His homework is unbelievably heavy, his exams are difficult and barely based on what we've learned. Lee Friedman is honestly a waste of tuition money. This class is only one credit, don't waste your time taking it with him.

I love Dr. Schech! Her lectures are so easy to follow along with and often pretty interesting, her exams are not hard, and she gives a lot of bonus questions on them. My friends with the other chem teachers were jealous of me

I don't know why people are giving her low ratings because she genuinely made CHEM easy to understand. If anything I thought she was going slow for many parts because she wanted us to understand it. I will say that the cherry on top though was definitely discussions because we worked through problems together and if you had any questions, you'd ask her. She made things so straightforward and easy, especially for her exams, she would provide study guides with topics you'd need to know which made studying easier. Overall, I would take her again, she was an amazing professor.

Gen Chem 1 is going to be a hard class for many because its chemistry, thats pretty much given. Dr. Stocker was pretty good with breaking down concepts into things that aren't chemistry related (like Legos) so students could understand them better, which def helped. However, occasionally, I felt like she skipped into things that I felt needed more background knowledge. That can be an easy fix by watching some Youtube though, but it definitely confused me in the moment. All in all, I don't believe the exams were unfair or INCREDIBLY difficult. Plus, she is usually good with giving some partial credit if you at least get somewhere with the exam questions. 
She has 3 exams, a final, and weekly homework due on Wednesday night. She doesn't add the homework grades until the very end which was not very helpful in determining your grade before the final. The curve is applied at the very end of the semester with the MINIMUM grade for an A- being an 85% in the class. However, these curve thresholds can be lowered depending on how bad the class averages are. She also gives a lot of her past exams with a couple answer keys for you to practice with. Plus, the discussion with Vince was super helpful, he basically summarized/reexplained the concepts we learned in class. 
All in all, Dr. Stocker is a good professor. She gives a lot of practice problem sets, old exams, and I do genuinely believe she wants you to do well. However, she does go fast and I feel like she skips over some background knowledge for the occasional concept.

Taking Dr. Schech for 131 was the best decision I made for my first semester of college. She was so nice and approachable, and never made you feel bad for asking a question. She was also so knowledgable and passionate about chem, so she made it interesting even to someone who doesn't like the subject. She taught in a very easy-to-understand way and used examples and analogies that made the topics easy to understand. I went to most of the lectures, even though she does record them and posts the notes. For taking notes, I do recommend an ipad and a note taking app like goodnotes. It made it so much easier to keep up in class because it was easy to import the diagrams and charts that she would use on her slides. I highly recommend using the textbook to study too, because it really did break down concepts well. The tests were also not too hard if you studied the extra material she gave. I personally thought the actual tests were pretty similar to the practice ones, maybe a little harder. A lot of my friends who had other professors really struggled through chem131, but for me it was really easy with Schech. If you can, take her!!

Lascio is a great, engaging lecturer, but his exams are incredibly difficult and not related to the material covered in lecture at all, which makes his style of teaching relatively unhelpful when preparing for exams. On top of this he's mentioned in lecture that he does not feel it's his job to teach us, which I guess is fair at a college level, but I feel like if I'm paying this much money to go to college I want a professor who wants to help us learn in lecture, not one who just expects us to learn everything on our own. The homework, lecture notes, and practice exams are all significantly easier than what he puts on the actual exams, so its difficult to prepare for them, and he also does not drop questions if the majority of the class gets them wrong. On our second midterm there was a problem that only three people got right in a 260 person lecture, but he did not drop the question or curve the exam. One of the best parts of taking him, however, is the curve at the end of the semester. Like most chem classes, it's based on your peers so it will change year by year, but it allowed me (and many others) to pass the class. He's the kind of prof that I wouldn't recommend, but I also wouldn't break down into tears having, as he's very approachable and responsive. I believe he's moving to a lab coordinator position, which I feel is a better fit for him anyway.

Quick helpful tip if you have him for 131! If he teaches you an exception to a rule, write it down because it'll be on the exam almost every time.

Disclaimer: I took this course in Fall 2024, and I’m writing this review after completing both Orgo I and Orgo II. First off, Dr. Dixon is really smart and genuinely knows how to explain difficult concepts clearly. That said, I’ll be honest—she can come off as a bit mean when answering questions during lecture, especially from students who don’t do well on exams. One review mentioned that she’s bipolar and I lowkey agree with that. In terms of course structure, there are three midterms, one final, and a bunch of homework assignments. The homework is very challenging and usually took me around 7 hours to complete, but you’re given a full week to do it. One frustrating thing is that sometimes Dr. Dixon doesn’t cover all of the homework material in lecture until just a couple of days before it’s due. Because of this, I often had to go to office hours to do well on the assignments. Personally, I hated office hours because they’re overcrowded and held in a really small room, but unfortunately, going is pretty much necessary if you want good homework grades. Dr. Dixon also runs something called Chemistry at Night (CAN), where she works through harder practice problems. The best part is that these sessions are recorded and posted online, so you can watch them on your own time. The homework and CAN sessions are easily the two best resources for doing well on exams. I felt that all of the midterms were very representative of the lecture, homework, and CAN material, though the last midterm was definitely the hardest. The final, on the other hand, was by far the easiest exam and I didn’t really have to learn anything new to do well on it. Another huge plus is the 10-point buffer added to exam scores. Honestly, most people who complain about this class fall into one of three categories: freshmen with ineffective study strategies, students who never took a rigorous science class in high school, or people who don’t go to lecture (which is a bad idea since lectures aren’t recorded). So if you want to do well, listen up: go to class, actually work through the homework problems (don’t use chatgpt), watch the CAN videos, and make a solid review sheet for each exam. This class is the single biggest reason I improved my study strategies, and it ultimately helped me earn As in both Orgo I and Orgo II.

I genuinely love Dr. Schech so much as a professor; it is difficult to put into words. Before this past semester, I had not taken a chemistry class in the last three years. Almost everything, barring the first two lectures or so, was completely new material that I had never encountered in my life, so to say that I was terrified for this class is an understatement. That said, Dr. Schech teaches so well that chemistry ended up being my best subject by far.

First of all, she doesn't just read off slides. Her lectures are super interactive, and she'll go through every one of her slides, taking notes with you, making sure to highlight important topics, explaining concepts in a multitude of ways so everyone understands, etc. She also uses a lot of visual examples when explaining topics that might get a little confusing if she were just verbally explaining (e.g., orbitals, hybridization, electron properties, etc.). In addition to her lectures being super helpful, she records and posts them after every class, so you can go back and rewatch them.

The exams for this class, in my opinion, were more than fair and never contained material that didn't match what we had learned throughout the course. Plus, she posted full-length practice exams a week before every exam (including the final) the were very helpful to help you prepare. Also, the discussion worksheets help a lot with this, too.

Overall, I really can't say enough about how great a professor Dr. Schech is. She is so sweet, easy to talk to, enthusiastic, and INCREDIBLY knowledgeable in not only the subject she teaches, but also HOW to teach it. 10/10 would absolutely recommend, especially anyone who might be concerned about gen chem like I was. Hope I can have her as a professor again.

Not an impossible class but definitely something you have to work for. Studying for tests less than two days before is not a good idea. It was hard to attend lectures because it was 8AM, I think if I attended more I could have done better. Be sure to utilize every resource he provides (ESPECIALLY the practice tests), because he doesn't provide many. The course and tests gets harder as the semester goes on, so make sure you don't lose any momentum.
Horrible at lecturing. most of the important stuff is skimmed over. Don't expect an easy time, most professors teaching chem will be better.

Please take Schech for Gen Chem 1 if you have the opportunity. Her class is so well organized, she gives you apt study materials, and she is just enjoyable to listen to. She makes it easy to skip lecture because she is so good about posting her notes and lectures, but you should go because she is a joy to be around. Her exams are very fair and the final too, as long as you do your practice.
Dr. Schech is an amazing lecturer, but is incredibly inflexible and unaccommodating.

- Very nice, answers all questions (only in person though, no email)
- Grades quickly
- Teaches the material very well
- She posts tons of practice test and practice problems (many of which also have answer keys) which are really good predictors of her tests
- There is mandatory homework and you do have to pay for the website to do that homework, but I found the homework extremely helpful
- Discussions don't take attendance and you could go to any of them. These were also helpful
- Go to GSS if you need extra help!

If there is any review you listen to, let it be this one. If there is ANY possible other professor you can take, I URGE you, BEG you to take any other option. Dr. Friedman is rude and runs through topics as if you have already learned them in depth. Yes, you should be expected to have a simple understanding of chemistry and remember things from high school, but the amount that I had to learn on my own was honestly diabolical. I spent probably over 10 hours a week on CHEM 131 (not including lab), simply by attending lectures, going to GSS twice a week, and going to office hours and discussions, doing the homework, and teaching myself. I am generally a straight-A student, and got an A+ in my chemistry class in high school. In this class, I worked my actual ass off for weeks, and didn't see the results I wanted since he would test us on the rare niche exceptions. I learned new things just by looking at his old exams. Be prepared to memorize the most unnecessary stuff and spend hours on the homework, while totally ruining your self-esteem. He is insulting and rude, going to his office hours did not help, instead it made me feel small and stupid. The ONLY pro is that his curve is very generous. I genuinely learned everything from Amy, the GSS leader, and Chad's prep on YouTube. I did not miss a single lecture, and it did not help. He is rude and cannot teach, though he clearly really does know what he's talking about. He blames his low averages on his students not trying, though that is not the case. I am literally begging you to take any other teacher. Studying with my friends who were in other Chemistry classes absolutely blew my mind since they didn't even need to know more than half the stuff that I had to know. Also, my TA was so rude and didn't help at all. In conclusion, you can definitely survive this class if you put in the work, but be prepared that it's not easy and that you might be questioning whether you are actually a good student or not. Make sure to take advantage of your resources and start studying as early as possible. Good luck.

Dr. Schech was an amazing teacher! her tests were ALWAYS fair and it is easy to do well based on just her lectures and what she teaches you. if you go to class/watch her lecture recordings and listen intently, you will do just fine! she often tells you exactly what will be tested, even down to the specific question archetypes

Chemistry is hard. Dr. Friedman is hard. Just because he is hard doesn't mean he does not care. It can be intimidating, but go to office hours and ask questions. At the end of one of our meetings we were just talking and we got to the conversation on why he makes his exams so challenging. He told me that he wants to differentiate the students who memorize for the exam and the ones who try to understand the ins and outs. Imagine if he were to do a problem during lecture such as 2 + 2 = 4 and on that exam theres a question that is 2 + 2 = ?. From this he isn't able to determine which students know why 2 + 2 = 4 and which ones just memorized that 2 + 2 = 4. With that being said his tests takes problems that were done in class and flip them, turn them, does literally anything to them to make it not look like the original and wants you to figure out where to start (that's the hardest part). To combat this do practice problems. The first three weeks of this class I literally drove myself insane from doing textbook problems, please save yourself and don't even open the textbook. Instead go to GSS, ESPECIALLY Amy (if she is still a GSS for Friedman) she is literally a life saver. There are so many FREE opportunities for you to succeed in this class. Go to lecture (suck it up you'll probably have to wake up earlier if not the same time for your job post-grad), go to office hours (especially before an exam, I typically would complete a past exam of his and go over anything that confused me and asked for him to walk me through it), GO TO GSS. The final was rough because he didn't give much material to work with like any past final exams, but that's department rules. I honestly feel really prepared going into orgo compared to some of my other friends who took different professors and honestly I would take Friedman again.

PLEASE take her. yes,  obv you need to put in effort if you want an A, but professor stump is on your side and wants you to succeed. lecture can be a bit boring sometimes and might feel slow but its honestly fine bc she has so many resources to help u succeed outside of lecture. i met with her 1:1 multiple times and those meetings were incredibly helpful. the one thing i wish she did is record lectures bc sometimes when studying the scanned notes can get a little confusing if you dont remember the exact context. the exams are really straightforward and i never got anything lower than an A. homework is online and is a good grade bump too. also def go to GSS if you can because those sessions were v helpful for working thru confusing concepts. basically if you have to take this class, take professor stump!

I really liked her, she taught very well and the homework really connected to the concepts we learned in class. I will say, she moves very fast so investing in a note taking app of some sort will be extremely helpful, as well as attending GSS and scheduling office hours. I personally believe she taught very well and made the concepts simple, coming from someone who hasn’t taken chemistry since sophomore year of high school and doesn’t remember anything. Exams were fair, very much based on what we learned in class, and she straight up tells you what you MUST know for the exams, such as crucial points like electron configuration exceptions or polyatomic ions and their charges. Overall she was a good professor for introduction to chemistry, I definitely recommended.

If there is any single review you listen to, let it be this one. If there is ANY other way to take this class, and I mean any other way, I urge you to take the other option. To establish some credibility, I would like to mention that I am an extremely hard worker and do what it takes to excel in a class. I am generally a straight-A student and received an A+ in my high school chemistry course. The number of hours and hours I spent on this class, from lectures, homework, GSS, and discussion, to end with a B+ is ridiculous (not saying a B+ is a bad grade, it's not, I just put in so much work). Dr. Friedman is a rude and impatient man. He teaches you concepts as if you should already know them, and going to his office hours doesn't help, as it seems as though he doesn't want to help you. Going through his old tests to study, I would often learn a new exception I didn't know, or get things wrong because he tests you on the smallest details. You cannot study with your friends who are in other chemistry classes because they have vastly different work than you. I tried studying with my friends, and they didn't even know half the stuff I was talking about. He also makes you memorize such unnecessary information, like the ENTIRE solubility chart. The only pro to his class is that his grade cutoffs are pretty generous. He doesn't record any lectures, which was fine with me as I went to every single one, but genuinely, lectures did not help. He runs through the material and gets impatient when questions are asked. I honestly never really felt prepared for his tests, despite going to GSS every single week and studying for 2 weeks in advance. Also, his handwriting is awful, and you're going to be left squinting at the board several times because he doesn't care to write things nicely for his students. If you are unfortunately stuck with him and are confused by concepts, the YouTube videos by Chad's Prep literally saved me. Make sure to make friends in this class so you guys can study together, go through his old exams, and go to GSS so you can actually learn the material. Also, I pray that your TA is nice. Mine was so rude and literally hated discussion and questions. Like, why are you a TA if you hate doing the things that the TA has to do lol. In conclusion, really try to avoid this professor if you don't want to add at least 10 hours of additional work per week to your life.

This course was extremely challenging and negatively impacted my mental health. Despite attending GSS, completing practice exams, and consistently studying, I struggled to score above a 60 on the exams. The exams felt significantly more difficult than the practice material and required a level of speed and depth that was hard to manage. If possible, I strongly recommend taking a different professor for General Chemistry.

As someone who didn't take any Organic Chem or AP Chem in high school, I was really nervous for this course. Throughout the semester, I learned that Dr. Friedman tells you everything you need to do to succeed. First week, he told us that we would need to do practice problems, COME TO LECTURE, go to GSS (guided study sessions), and do all practice exams. I did all of this and ended with a 93 in the course. Fortunately, I am someone who really enjoys math, so that part was easy (ish) for me to understand with practice. There is absolutely not a topic in this course that you can just "know". You must know the ins and outs and manipulations for literally EVERYTHING. I would say that GSS is going to be your saving grace, especially with Amy. The exams, in my opinion, were fair if you studied at least a week in advance and did all of the practice exams and worked on everything he throws at you. I thought the final was unfair and I felt unprepared, but the curve helped. Do the best you can to do well on all the midterms so then you have a lot of wiggle room as you enter the final.

Amazing professor! So glad I took chem131 with her. Her lectures are very helpful and she gives lots of analogies and examples for concepts that will appear on the tests. The tests were a lot like the practice exams and as long as you do well on those you should do fine on the exams. She’s also genuinely such a sweet lady and is very approachable.

If you can take any other professor, please do. 

While his lectures are easy to follow and he is a good professor overall, his exams are extremely hard, with the average grades being 50%. If you ask him a question in lecture, he will give you an attitude back in front of everyone but claim that he's not giving an attitude. 

Overall, if you're willing to put in the work, which will require a lot of separate practice and textbook practice, because I didn't find that the two hour homework helped much, you should be fine.

Dr. Schech is a phenomenal lecturer and the best CHEM131 professor by far! When she goes through lectures, she uses lots of analogies, makes things simple to understand, and doesn't do as much historical background and more useless stuff like some of the other professors do. She records every lecture, and posts her notes too which are useful! Overall, I found that most midterms, besides the last, and the final were all super easy. On top of that, she gives you plenty of resources in discussion with the TA to practice, and even a practice exam with a key. She curves the class too! She truly sets everyone up for success and is such a positive light for everyone.
honestly he rly isnt so bad.

Found her lecture style to fit my style of learning very well. She was very nice and used lots of non-chemistry examples to help you understand the material. There is weekly homework, but it was actually helpful to do and grades very quickly. Gave lots of example problems and even practice exams (old exams) with keys to help you study. The only downside is she only gives you a periodic table for the exam, so you had to memorize everything else, and you can't use a notecard while for other professors for this class, their students had to memorize less content, and it was given to them. Lectures weren't recorded but attendance isn't mandatory, so you'd need to get notes from a friend if you miss class. The discussions weren't mandatory, BUT I highly recommend going to them as the TA when I took the class was extremely helpful and went over content that helped you understand it better. You also could go to any of the discussions as long as they had space. There were 3 exams and a cumulative final with no drops. Overall, I really enjoyed learning from her, but you do need to put in the work to get a good grade in this class.

he's a really nice person and does really want to help, but genuinely is a very physics based teacher, and will teach as so. it makes it super difficult to learn chemistry, as it seems he wants you to know chem on a deeper level than you're capable of learning in the period of time you have for class. this class legit made me realize that i didnt want to be a chem major and i changed majors mid year. if you spend all your time studying and legit dedicate yourself all week to this class you'd do fine, but other teachers for 131 were definitely better.

Lascio is a really nice professor. I kinda skipped most of the classes, so I don't really know how he is as a lecturer, but he responds super fast and very nicely to emails. He definitely cares about his students and their success. For final grades, he put a lot of thought and consideration into the most fair way for rounding them, and the curve was pretty generous. I didn't do that great in this class since I didn't study as often or go to class as I should've, but I still think Lascio is a great professor for this class. I do agree with one of the other reviews, which said that he likes putting exceptions rules on exams.

Definitely the best professor to take CHEM131 with!! I have friends who took other professors and I can say this with conviction. The bad reviews are fixating on the fact that test averages were pretty low and yeah, 50-60% isn't GREAT. What they're leaving out is that at the end of the year, as long as you had a 50% in the class, you were guaranteed to pass. He also is very clear that even if you're failing the class, as long as you can pass the final exam with at least a C-, you'll pass the class! He implied that this would be hard, but not because the final was especially evil in difficulty. If you've failed the three midterm exams, it's obviously going to take a lot of work to pass the final?? Not many professors have this policy in place at all.

The questions on exams are application-based mostly. I wouldn't call them "trick" questions per se, but you definitely cannot get by on just memorizing the equations and looking for keywords, which is what I think a lot of people tried to do. He was very clear about this from the start of the class; you can't just churn out procedural practice problems for this class. His exams rely on a grasp of the actual theory, but it's not like he leaves you to figure this out yourself. The homeworks he assigns (on Pearson for our class), while challenging, are your BEST bet to learning the material. A lot of students in my class used AI to just finish them and get 100% (they are graded for accuracy and all of them add to a midterm grade) but you also get three attempts each. The homework problems are PURPOSEFULLY MORE DIFFICULT THAN THE EXAM QUESTIONS. As long as you can solidly do the homework, you're fine! He was very clear about the difficulty and value of the homeworks as well.

He also gives out a practice exam and study guide a week before each exam, which I was fine with (and found to be standard). While the practice exam might be a little (emphasis on a little) easier, I think it was very representative of the types of exam questions. Timing yourself taking it is a very valuable resource. Also, on each study guide, he'll make it clear what we need to memorize and what will be given on the formula sheet! We also get the formula sheet in advance.

TL;DR Lascio is a great professor and cares about your success. I did not have to dedicate more than 2-3 hours/week to the homeworks (which I also used to study). This class is not an easy A by any means, but you'll get out of it what you put in. Don't use AI, do the homeworks, listen to what he SAYS, not just what he WRITES, and be friendly with him. He's a cool dude.
Leah was a great TA! She answers emails quickly and is very approachable. 10/10 no notes
explains well and answers questions

Yes, this class really is that bad. Listen to your peers who tell you to never take this professor. If you don't already have a lot of prior knowledge and a really good understanding of the subject (gen chem), do not take this class. I attended almost every lecture, and for the ones I missed, I reviewed the notes online. I tried on-campus tutoring, GSS sessions, and watched a ton of videos online. The way he teaches is not beginner-friendly, and he goes too fast. I believed I had a good understanding of each concept (all the practice problems in the videos I was getting 100%) until I opened the tests. If you ever need to take a general chemistry class, either take it in the summer at a community college, or with a professor whose average rating is not a 2.6.
Don't take this class unless you already know everything about general chemistry.

name: CHEM131
title: Chemistry I - Fundamentals of General Chemistry
description: Prerequisite: Must have math eligibility of MATH120 or higher. Corequisite: CHEM132. Recommended: For Science majors. Credit only granted for: CHEM103, CHEM131, CHEM135, CHEM153 or CHEM146. Formerly: CHEM103. An overview of the Periodic Table, inorganic substances, ionic and covalent bonding, bulk properties of materials, chemical equilibrium, and quantitative chemistry. CHEM131 is the first course in a four-semester sequence for students majoring in the sciences, other than Chemistry and Biochemistry majors.
